thread:
alex: Heads up — staging canary p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms after merge 8f3c2a2 around 10:30PT. Canary paused by rollout. CI perf job also failed. Anyone on bisect?
maria: I saw it too. Heatmap shows bigger batching windows + KV eviction churn. Quick topo: kernel selector now uses `ceil(batch_size / 64) * 64` rounding in commit 8f3c2a2 — maybe changed from floor. Could cause small batches to use larger kernel.
ryan: :eyes: That rounding change rings a bell. I can start a git bisect on the staging branch. Need a repro script; CI job is flakey locally.
alex: Thanks. I saved the perf snapshot and flamegraph to the staging run: https://redwood.metrics/staging/shot/2026-03-17/abc123 :point_up: key lines in flamegraph show 40% more time in `select_kernel`.
dina: Can you paste the small profiler snippet? Also what's the failing CI job name?
alex: CI job: `ci/perf/e2e-staging-latency`. Profiler snippet (top 10):
```
select_kernel 40.3%
apply_attention 18.7%
kv_cache_eviction 12.1%
batching_router 9.6%
others 19.3%
```
ci-bot: Alert: build 2214 `ci/perf/e2e-staging-latency` failed at 1958765400. Logs: https://ci.redwood/build/2214
ryan: I'll run git bisect with an automated perf check. Command I'm about to run:
```
git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad
git bisect bad 8f3c2a2
git bisect good 7a1b9c0
git bisect run ./scripts/check_staging_perf.sh
```
Script will run a minimal workload and pass if p95 < 200ms.
maria: Note: `check_staging_perf.sh` needs access to KV fixtures — add `--kv-size 10MB` or it skews results.
ryan: @maria good call. I'll update script. Also to speed up local repro use `TEST_SEQ=256 MAKE_IT_FAST=1` env vars.
alex: If bisect hits flaky tests, we should fall back to manual bisection by cherry-picking suspected commits: 8f3c2a2 -> 8f3c2a2^ etc. Also consider reverting kernel selector rounding first as a quick rollback.
dina: :thumbsup: Can I take the revert candidate? I can make a PR that restores the previous batching rounding and run a canary.
ryan: Bisect run started. Posting progress every 5 mins.
ci-bot: Bisect step 1/18 — tested commit 8e92f4b (good).
ryan: Step 7/18 shows commit 8f3c2a2 is the first bad. It changes `kernel_selector.cpp` rounding logic + adds heuristics for tiny batches. Logs: `kernel_selector: rounding up leads to choosing 256 kernel instead of 64 for batch=70`
alex: Confirmed locally by running microbench: `bench_kernel_choice --batch=70` shows 2.8x slower path when rounding up.
maria: That matches spike. The KV cache churn is secondary: larger kernels increase memory stride and cause more frequent kv evictions under our eviction policy.
dina: I'll open the revert PR now and tag @eng-runtime for quick review. If tests pass I'll deploy a hotfix canary.
alex: Also add a unit test for `kernel_selector` to assert boundary behavior around multiples of 64.
ryan: Final note: add telemetry to console to log `kernel_size_chosen` per request for 24h after hotfix so we can validate no regressions across traffic patterns.
